title: Tenant Manager backend: CRUD, soft remove/restore, transactional template seeding + partition creation
objective: Port the Tenant Manager API: cross-tenant, global-permission-bound tenant list/create/get/update, soft remove and restore — where tenant creation transactionally copies the global default reference template into the tenant AND creates that tenant's partitions via the SQL function — all audited (P-02, section 12 Tenant Manager).
scope: GET /api/v1/tenants (list incl. status filter), POST /api/v1/tenants, GET /api/v1/tenants/{id}, PUT /api/v1/tenants/{id}
POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/remove (soft, status Removed), POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/restore — audited, permission-bound

Tenant creation transaction: insert tenant -> call partition-creation function for all partitioned tables -> copy default_reference_items into reference_items -> create default tenant_settings row -> audit — all-or-nothing
Removed tenants excluded from normal switching surfaces (membership lists /me) but visible to authorized Internal users
implementation_details: Routes are cross-tenant: no X-Tenant-Id; guarded by the global tenant-management permissions (mirror reference keys); route classification per T-013 convention.
Name required; contact fields optional; validation via zod mirroring FluentValidation rules.

Partition creation + template copy inside one Kysely transaction on the app/owner path that has DDL rights for partition DDL — NOTE: partition creation is DDL; verify the app role may execute the SECURITY DEFINER partition function (grant EXECUTE), else route through a definer function — document the choice.
Restore re-activates; historical data remains intact (soft-remove only, N-09).
Audit entries for create/update/remove/restore/template edits with before/after payloads (P-13).
Global template PUT validates guarded-status invariants (reporting categories, canonical keys, terminal flags).

integration: Create tenant: reference lists seeded from template, partitions exist for every partitioned table, settings row created — atomically (induced failure rolls back everything)
Soft remove hides tenant from normal switching; restore brings it back; both audited
Permission matrix: caller without tenant-management permission -> 403; anonymous -> 401
Template PUT rejects invalid reporting category / duplicate canonical key; template edit audited
Contract check: DTO field names match reference API
e2e: Tenant Manager spec adapted in T-043 (create/edit/remove/restore through the existing UI)

findings.description: The task's central production fix - wiring `rbac: defaultRbacDeps()` into both composition roots so requirePermission routes stop failing closed with 500 - has NO regression guard, and the task's own history claims one exists ('production wiring asserted by auth-wiring.test.ts source-grep per its existing convention'). auth-wiring.test.ts pins only the auth, tenancy, and me slots; it never mentions rbac. defaultRbacDeps' doc comment (src/server/domains/rbac/index.ts) also states 'tests/integration/auth-wiring.test.ts pins that they do', which is false.
findings.evidence: DEMONSTRATED GREEN-GATE SURVIVOR: evaluator removed `rbac: defaultRbacDeps(),` and its import from api/v1/[[...segments]].ts, then ran the full gates - typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, npm test 55 files / 873 passed / 0 skipped exit 0. Under that regression every requirePermission route in production (the entire Tenant Manager surface, the global-template routes, and every guarded route later tasks add) would return 500 while the whole suite stays green. File restored and confirmed sha256-identical (fad7d1f6...). The wiring itself IS real and works: evaluator drove a one-shot probe building the app with the exact default* deps chain of the production roots - tenants.view holder got 200 on GET /api/v1/tenants, a no-permission caller got 403, not 500.

Correct the defaultRbacDeps doc comment so it becomes true.

findings.description: The four-stage atomicity proof cannot distinguish WHICH connection the tenant.created audit row is written on. A regression that writes the audit via the pool (`writeAudit(deps.db, ...)` instead of `writeAudit(trx, ...)`) inside createTenant survives the whole tenants suite green: the stage-4 trigger still raises on the separate connection, the error still propagates, the transaction still rolls back, and assertNothingPersisted still holds. The unpinned residual behavior is an audit row that commits independently of the creation transaction (a false audit record if the enclosing commit subsequently fails, and a row briefly visible for a tenant that does not yet exist).
findings.evidence: DEMONSTRATED: evaluator applied the writeAudit(deps.db) mutant to src/server/domains/tenants/service.ts createTenant and ran tenants.test.ts - 26/26 passed, exit 0. Restored sha256-identical (3f34f862...). Control: a swallowed-seeding-failure mutant in the same function WAS killed by the template-seeding stage (1 targeted failure), so the stages do discriminate genuine partial-creation regressions; only the executor-choice axis is blind.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the stage-4 audit trigger transaction-aware: raise the induced failure ONLY when the fixture-named tenant row is visible from within the trigger's own transaction (`exists (select 1 from tenants where name like 't016-fault-audit-%')` alongside the existing new.action/name check). Same-transaction audit writes see the uncommitted tenant row and fail as today (green baseline); a separate-connection write does not see it, the audit commits, creation returns 201 instead of the expected 500, and the test goes red - killing the mutant with a two-line trigger change and pinning audit-inside-the-transaction (AC-024/P-13 intent).
findings.resolution: Added a transaction-visibility test that discriminates on the executor axis the atomicity suite was blind to. A BEFORE INSERT trigger on audit_log raises only when the not-yet-committed tenant row is INVISIBLE to the inserting connection - true from a separate connection (deps.db), false from inside the creation transaction (trx). PROVEN: swapping writeAudit(trx) -> writeAudit(deps.db) previously left 26/26 green; it now fails that test (1 failed / 26 passed), restored byte-identical. The test asserts 201 as a positive control, so a trigger that fired spuriously would show up as the mutant's own 500 signature.
findings.summary: The four-stage atomicity proof cannot distinguish WHICH connection the tenant.created audit row is written on.

findings.description: The composition-root wiring pin added for F-016-1 covers the rbac slot only; the `tenants` and `globalTemplate` slots - the wiring of THIS task's own delivered surface - remain unpinned. Both are optional in buildApp (app.ts declares `tenants?:` / `globalTemplate?:` and registers the routes only inside `if (deps.tenants)` / `if (deps.globalTemplate)`), so a root that drops either slot ships a production API where the entire Tenant Manager (or global-template) surface answers 404 while every gate stays green. F-016-1's suggested_fix explicitly proposed pinning these two slots alongside rbac ('preferably pin the tenants/globalTemplate slots the same way while there'); the resolution pinned rbac only.
findings.evidence: DEMONSTRATED FULL-GREEN SURVIVOR (same class as F-016-1): evaluator removed `tenants: defaultTenantsDeps(),` and its import from api/v1/[[...segments]].ts and ran the gates - npm test 55 files / 876 passed / 0 skipped exit 0, typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0. Under that regression every /api/v1/tenants route 404s in deployed production. The Vercel root is never executed by any test, and T-043's future e2e will drive scripts/dev/serve-api.ts, not this file - so the auth-wiring source pin is the ONLY guard the deployed entrypoint can ever have. Restored byte-identical (sha256 fad7d1f6...), auth-wiring 10/10 green afterwards. globalTemplate shares the identical mechanism (optional slot, conditional registration, no pin); not separately mutation-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add two more `it.each(COMPOSITION_ROOTS)` cases to auth-wiring.test.ts mirroring the four existing pins: `buildApp\(\{[^}]*tenants:\s*defaultTenantsDeps\(\)` and `buildApp\(\{[^}]*globalTemplate:\s*defaultGlobalTemplateDeps\(\)`. Establish the convention that every future domain task adds its slot's pin in the same change that wires it, so this class of survivor stops recurring per-domain.
findings.resolution: Added both missing slot pins to tests/integration/auth-wiring.test.ts, mirroring the four existing it.each(COMPOSITION_ROOTS) cases: tenants -> defaultTenantsDeps() and globalTemplate -> defaultGlobalTemplateDeps(). Suite 10 -> 14 tests. FIVE mutants run, all KILLED (1 failed / 13 passed each): tenants-slot removal from BOTH roots, globalTemplate-slot removal from BOTH roots, and a hollow-pin variant that keeps the import and drops ONLY the wiring line (proving the buildApp({...}) regex is load-bearing, not the toContain). Both roots restored byte-identical (api/v1 sha256 fad7d1f6..., serve-api sha256 15e9ef0b...). METHOD NOTE, recorded because it nearly produced a false negative of the opposite kind: the first mutation pass reported the two serve-api.ts mutants as SURVIVORS. They were not - the mutation never applied. serve-api.ts wires buildApp at one level shallower indentation (4 spaces) than the Vercel root (6), so the fixed-indent grep -v matched nothing and the file was unchanged. Re-run with a line-count assertion proving each mutant actually modified the file: both KILLED. A mutant that silently fails to apply looks exactly like a passing gate, which is the same false-green shape this task has been fighting; mutation runs should assert the target file changed before trusting a green result.

ATOMICITY PROVEN AT FOUR STAGES against the real DB (partition function raising; live template corrupted; BEFORE INSERT trigger on tenant_settings; BEFORE INSERT trigger on audit_log), each asserting no tenant row, no partitions, no reference rows, no settings row and no audit row - located via the identity value the rolled-back insert consumed, since the name is gone. Triggers name-scoped to this suite's fixtures so concurrent suites cannot be hit; every injection reverted in `finally` and followed by a SUCCESSFUL create so the assertions cannot be satisfied by a broken database. Pre-transaction duplicate-name rejection additionally asserts the identity sequence did not advance. Partition routing asserts a partition exists for EVERY catalog-discovered LIST(tenant_id) parent and that seeded rows report tableoid::regclass = reference_items_p<id>, not _default. 9 mutants all killed with positive controls in both suites. Orchestrator resolved F-016-1 and F-016-2, both proven by reproducing the evaluator's survivors. WHILE FIXING, DISCOVERED AND FIXED A SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT owned by T-008's generator: `npm run db:types` wrote the CLI's output verbatim, and `supabase gen types` emits PARTITION tables. Partitions are created at runtime by create_tenant_partitions whenever a tenant is created, so any tenant-creating test changed the generator's output. Two consequences, both observed for real: (1) db-types-drift.test.ts's FIRST case invokes db:types WITHOUT --check, overwriting the committed generated files from the live DB - after T-016's tenant tests that baked leads_p44-style partitions into the schema, breaking T-008's everySchemaTableIsListed guard so `npm run typecheck` failed after a full `npm test` with nothing in the suite output pointing at the cause; (2) db:types --check then reported phantom drift, which is why ci:test failed 3 tests while npm test passed. Fixed at the ROOT in scripts/db/generate-types.ts: partitions are now queried (relispartition = true) and stripped from the CLI output before writing, matching the filtering the overrides and tenant-table queries already did. Also made the drift suite's first case snapshot/restore both generated files, since it is the only case that writes without --check. VERIFIED: with 20 partition tables deliberately present, db:types --check exits 0; typecheck is clean AFTER a full npm test; ci:test 876/876, 0 skipped, exit 0.
